Task 1.5: WHY morphology works¶

  • Erosion is a local minimum filter (shrinks white regions, removes small bright noise)[cite: 1].
  • Dilation is a local maximum filter (grows white regions, fills small dark gaps)[cite: 1].
  • Opening (erosion → dilation) removes small noise while preserving overall shape/size[cite: 1]. I would use this to clean up "salt" noise from a camera feed before running object detection.
  • Closing (dilation → erosion) fills small holes without shrinking the object[cite: 1]. I would use this to connect broken segments of an object mask (like text or lane lines).

Task 2.5: WHY alpha/beta and histograms matter¶

The formula is new_pixel = alpha * pixel + beta.

  • Alpha (contrast gain) stretches or compresses the histogram spread around its mean[cite: 1].
  • Beta (brightness offset) shifts the whole histogram left or right[cite: 1]. A narrow histogram indicates low contrast, while clipping at 0 or 255 indicates over/under-exposure[cite: 1]. This diagnostic view helps judge if an image needs pre-processing before being fed to face/object detectors.

Task 3.5: WHY YuNet¶

YuNet is a compact, modern CNN-based detector (default in OpenCV 5.0) trained on diverse, in-the-wild faces[cite: 1]. This gives it strong generalization to profile views, occlusion, and small/blurry faces, while returning 5-point landmarks in one forward pass[cite: 1]. The score_threshold trades off missed detections against false positives; I would use 0.9 for a secure access camera (to avoid false positives) and 0.5 for an offline photo-tagging tool (to catch every possible face)[cite: 1].

Task 4.5: WHY YOLO generalises¶

YOLO's single-stage, grid-based design divides the image into a grid, directly regressing bounding boxes and class probabilities in one forward pass, followed by Non-Max Suppression to remove duplicate detections[cite: 1]. The 'nano' variant used here prioritizes speed (FPS) over absolute accuracy compared to larger models (s/m/l/x), making it ideal for edge devices. It can detect 80 classes without hand-tuning because it leverages massive pretraining on the diverse COCO dataset[cite: 1].

import time
import io
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from IPython.display import display, Javascript
from google.colab.output import eval_js

# JavaScript to initialize webcam and stream frames
def video_stream_js():
    js = Javascript('''
        var video;
        var div = null;
        var stream;
        var captureCanvas;

        function removeDom() {
           if (stream) {
               stream.getVideoTracks()[0].stop();
           }
           if (video) video.remove();
           if (div) div.remove();
           video = null;
           div = null;
        }

        async function initCamera() {
          if (div !== null) {
            removeDom();
          }

          div = document.createElement('div');
          div.style.border = '2px solid black';
          div.style.padding = '10px';
          div.style.width = '640px';
          div.style.background = '#333';

          video = document.createElement('video');
          video.style.display = 'block';
          video.width = 640;
          video.height = 480;
          video.autoplay = true;
          video.playsInline = true;

          stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({video: { facingMode: "user" }});
          div.appendChild(video);
          video.srcObject = stream;

          document.body.appendChild(div);
          await new Promise((resolve) => video.onloadedmetadata = resolve);

          captureCanvas = document.createElement('canvas');
          captureCanvas.width = 640;
          captureCanvas.height = 480;
        }

        async function captureFrame() {
          var ctx = captureCanvas.getContext('2d');
          ctx.drawImage(video, 0, 0, 640, 480);
          return captureCanvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.8);
        }
    ''')
    display(js)

def js_to_image():
    # Capture frame via browser javascript
    image_bytes = eval_js('captureFrame()')
    header, encoded = image_bytes.split(',')
    decoded = io.BytesIO(np.frombuffer(io.BytesIO(eval_js('atob("' + encoded + '")').encode('latin-1')).read(), dtype=np.uint8))
    img = cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(decoded.read(), dtype=np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    return img

# Register the JS functions in the browser context first
video_stream_js()

# Wait brief moment for setup, then initialize camera
time.sleep(1)
eval_js('initCamera()')

# Display target for live output
img_display = display(display_id=True)
frame_count = 0
start_time = time.time()

try:
    while True:
        frame = js_to_image()
        if frame is None:
            break

        img_h, img_w = frame.shape[:2]

        # 1. Morphological Pre-cleaning (Optional/Light)
        kernel = np.ones((3,3), np.uint8)
        clean_frame = cv2.morphologyEx(frame, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel)

        # 2. YuNet Face Detection
        detector.setInputSize((img_w, img_h))
        _, faces = detector.detect(clean_frame)
        if faces is not None:
            for face in faces:
                box = list(map(int, face[:4]))
                cv2.rectangle(frame, box, (0, 255, 0), 2)
                cv2.putText(frame, 'Face', (box[0], box[1]-10), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 255, 0), 2)

        # 3. YOLO Object Detection
        results = model(clean_frame, verbose=False)
        frame = results[0].plot(img=frame)

        # FPS Calculation
        frame_count += 1
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        fps = frame_count / elapsed
        cv2.putText(frame, f'FPS: {fps:.1f}', (20, 40), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 1, (0, 0, 255), 2)

        # Output to Colab live frame
        _, encoded_img = cv2.imencode('.jpg', frame)
        img_display.update(Image.open(io.BytesIO(encoded_img)))

except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("Webcam stream stopped by user.")
finally:
    eval_js('removeDom()')

Webcam stream stopped by user.

Task 5.4: Final Results Comparison Table¶

Technique Type What It Detects Lighting Robustness Approx. FPS Best Use Case
Morphology Classical Shapes, Noise Very Low ~1000+ Pre-cleaning sensor noise
Bitwise / Hist Classical Masks, Exposure Low ~1000+ ROI extraction, contrast fixing
YuNet Deep Learning Faces & Landmarks High ~30-60 Biometric security, anonymization
YOLOv8n Deep Learning 80 COCO Classes High ~15-45 Traffic monitoring, retail analytics

Task 5.5: Reflection¶

Combining classical morphological pre-processing with deep-learning detection (YuNet + YOLO) gives the best accuracy-to-compute trade-off for real-time monitoring[cite: 1]. The morphology cleanly handles static sensor noise at near-zero compute cost, saving the deep models from hallucinating false positives. If deploying on a low-power edge device, I would stick to yolov8n and increase the YuNet score_threshold to save compute. For a cloud server, I would upgrade to yolov8s or yolov8m for higher accuracy at a distance[cite: 1].
